tasks.evidence-before: Measured on the pre-fix blob (`git show 5aa6752^:benchmark/tinytitan_rdadvise_ab.py`), in a scratch copy, with no model and no server. (1) `python3 -c "import old_driver"` reached `subprocess.Popen` for the `default` arm and only the scratch guard stopped it: `RuntimeError: opened a real benchmark log at import: .../tinytitan_rd_default.log`, exit 1. Importing the module launched a model server, waited 120 s on /health, sent two 512-token streamed requests, killed the server, and did it again for the `off` arm -- the run nobody asked for, and the reason no suite existed. (2) The empty-capture case: a server that printed no `cb1_ms=` line (a renamed footer, an env var the release CLI dropped, a build that lost the counter) still produced `--- off ---` followed by nothing and exit 0, because `run()` returned `None` and nothing in the file looked at the three lists it had built. A reader could not distinguish "rdadvise off changed nothing" from "the instrument measured nothing", and the section header asserted the arm existed. (3) A server that died before /health answered took `sys.exit(1)` from inside `run()`, which killed the whole A/B on the first arm without reporting the second. (4) `MODEL = str(DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH)` at :23 hardcoded the model, so `TINYTITAN_BENCH_MODEL` was ignored here: the three sibling sweeps that name their model through it (`tinytitan_overlap_measure.py:40`, `tinytitan_slots_ab.py:26`, `tinytitan_knob_sweep.py:36`) read it and pass the result as `server_command`'s `model=` argument, and this driver passed the constant instead, so it launched the default path whatever the operator exported. (5) `env["TINYTITAN_RDADVISE_POLICY"] = "off"` was written for the `off` arm only; the `default` arm inherited the parent environment, so running the A/B from a shell that already exported `TINYTITAN_RDADVISE_POLICY=off` (or any other policy) made the arm labelled `default` run that policy, and the printed header is the only record of what the arm was. `sources/TinyTitanLib/ServerModelSession+Loading.swift:198` reads the env var *ahead of* the loaded config, which is what makes the inheritance effective rather than cosmetic. (6) The docstring promised "Interleaved fresh servers"; :102-103 runs `default` then `off`, once each, in a fixed order -- an interleaved design would alternate arms across repeats, and the file does neither.
tasks.fix-summary: Nothing at module scope but constants: `MODES`, `PORT`, `MAX_TOKENS`, `PROMPT` and the `CHANNELS` table (each channel's marker substring *and* the string a reader needs if it is absent), with the driver behind `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`. `bench_model()` takes `TINYTITAN_BENCH_MODEL` and falls back to `DEFAULT_MODEL_PATH`, so the driver now points where its siblings point. `arm_environment(mode, base)` validates the arm name (`ValueError` on anything else), sets the two stats env vars, and is the only place the policy is decided: `off` sets `TINYTITAN_RDADVISE_POLICY=off`, `default` *pops* it, so an inherited value cannot silently become the control arm. The health wait and the two-request loop moved into `tinytitan_profile.py` (`wait_for_health`, which returns False only when the process exited and True on a still-alive timeout; `request_twice`) -- `tinytitan_overlap_measure.py`'s private copies of both were deleted and its call sites point at the shared ones, so AUD-225's driver keeps its behaviour and loses its duplication. `run()` opens its log with `with`, terminates in a `finally`, and returns the capture or `None` for a dead arm. `verdict(arms)` prints, per arm: `ARM FAILED: {mode} -- the server never answered /health` and exit 1 for a dead arm; a header that carries each channel's line count (`--- off (generation 2 lines, runner 0 lines, kernel total 1 line) ---`) so a partial run reads as partial; and `NOT MEASURED: {mode} -- no log line contained {marker!r}` with exit 1 for an empty section. `main()` refuses any argument with exit 2 and usage naming both arms and the 512-token length, then prints one line of plan (`rdadvise A/B: <model>, 512 tokens, one fresh server per arm`) before the arms. The docstring now says what the driver does (one fresh server per arm, in `MODES` order, not interleaved), which env vars it sets and which it clears, and what an arm that measured nothing prints. The A/B *numbers* are unchanged and not produced here: running it is a model run, which stays the operator's to schedule.

(5) The failed-row line read `cold=None load=Nones ttft=Nones tok/s=None tokens=None content=Nonech reasoning=Nonech`, because :167 prints the keys :147-148 set only on the success path, with an `s` appended to `None`.
tasks.fix-summary: Nothing at module scope but constants and the default base URL. `parse_int`, `parse_prompts`, `parse_runs` and `parse_config` take the environment as an argument and are called from `main()`, so the driver is importable before it is configured; each refusal is a `ConfigError` naming its variable and its value (`MAXTOK='abc' is not an integer`, `RUNS row 0=[...] is not [id, engine, label, quant] -- four fields`), and `main()` prints `REFUSED: ...` and returns **2**. The matrix is planned before the first request (`{n} rows planned: {runs} model x {prompts} prompt x {repeats} repeat against {base}`); a plan of zero prints `NOT MEASURED: the matrix planned no request` and returns **1**; every row is counted ok or failed as it is written, and the run ends `"{ok} ok, {failed} failed -- {written} of {planned} rows written"`, returning **1** if any row failed or the count does not match the plan, **0** only when every planned row came back ok. `load_s`/`cold` are set to `None` on every row before the request and printed through `shown()`, which renders `n/a` where the run never reached a value, so a failure no longer looks like a measurement of `Nones`. The catch-all stays -- a URLError mid-matrix must not lose the rows already written -- but it now records the row *and* fails the run. `warm()` and `measure()` are unchanged except that `measure` takes `maxtok`, so the parsed value reaches the request body instead of the module default; `post()` is the one seam every request goes through, and the parsed `PORT` reaches the URL it builds.

tasks.category: validation: the wire bounded four sampling knobs and passed the fifth straight through
tasks.file_line: sources/TinyTitanLib/OpenAIRequestValidator.swift:207-222
tasks.title: HTTP accepts a presence_penalty the CLI refuses, and applies it -- a different completion, no error
tasks.discovered-by: Phase D sweep back onto the Swift side, along the sampling-parameter path (wire -> facade -> engine validation) after a dozen closes in shell and python: every generation knob the wire touches, checked at each of the three layers rather than at the one the report named.
tasks.evidence-before: `OpenAIRequestValidator.validate` bounds temperature (0...2), top_p (>0, <=1), top_k (1...256) and repetition_penalty (>=1) and then assigns `presencePenalty: request.presencePenalty ?? effectiveSampling.presencePenalty` with no check. The engine's `GenerationConfig.validate()` asks only `presencePenalty.isFinite`, so nothing downstream refused either; and the CLI's `--presence-penalty` has refused anything outside OpenAI's -2...2 since v5.10, so the wire accepted a request the flag rejects. It is not an ignored field: `Sampler.applyPenaltiesInPlace` subtracts the value once per distinct id already in the history, so 100 takes every token the model has used out of contention and the answer comes from the rest of the vocabulary. Measured by the test before the repair (/tmp/aud254-red.log, exit 1, 38 tests 1 issue at OpenAIValidationTests.swift:494:32): `failure.envelope` -> nil for presence_penalty 2.5, ie validate() returned a config carrying 2.5 instead of throwing. The three published rows all sit inside the range (house 0, thinking 0, Qwen3.8 instruct 1.5), so no shipped default can be refused by the new cap.
tasks.evidence-after: The guard is in, and the whole test passes: `swift test --no-parallel --filter OpenAIValidationTests` -- 38 tests in 3 suites, exit 0 (/tmp/aud254-gated.log), covering 2.5 / -2.5 / 100 refused with param `presence_penalty` and the boundary values -2 / 1.5 / 2 accepted and still passing `generationConfig.validate()`. Full package suite serially: 7 target runs, 1734 tests in 253 suites, exit 0 (/tmp/aud254-full2.log). Gates as `bash tools/lint.sh <mode>`, each exit 0: swift-format, swiftlint, func-length, file-length, test-skip, test-hollow, docs (83 documents against 18 gates, 155 ledger commit references resolved). No model run -- the operator's TinyTitanServer holds the only live model process and the preflight forbids a second; nothing fetched; nothing pushed.
tasks.fix-evidence: Two mutants, each killed by a different half of the test. (1) Widen the range to -2...3: the wire loop fails (/tmp/aud254-mutant.log, exit 1) on the 2.5 row, so the bound is the one asserted, not a value that happens to reject. (2) Drop the `rules == .wire` gate (replace with `if true`): exit 1, 1 issue at OpenAIValidationTests.swift:478:6 in aPresencePenaltyOutsideTheOpenAIRangeIsRefusedAsBadRequest -- the `.local` assertion is what fails, which is the point: the facade's exemption is pinned, so the cap cannot silently become a library contract. The validator was restored from a copy taken after the last edit (/tmp/aud254-fixed2.swift) rather than `git checkout --`, and `git diff --stat` before the commit showed only the four intended files.
tasks.sibling-note: Same family, other layers, measured rather than assumed. Four negatives: (a) the engine's own validate() already refuses temperature > 0 with topK == nil and topP < 1 (full-vocabulary nucleus is not implemented), so a top_k=0 request the wire accepts reaches a deliberate engine refusal, not a silent change -- not filed; (b) a non-finite presence_penalty never reaches the validator at all, Foundation's JSONDecoder throws dataCorrupted for a number not representable in the target Float (measured: `1e39`), so an isFinite wire guard would be dead code -- not filed; (c) the Anthropic and Responses mappers route through the same validate(chatRequest, for:) and so inherit the cap rather than needing their own -- checked, and the Responses path is the one that would have needed a second guard; (d) MTP/speculative decode carries no presence penalty of its own. The sweep's hit was in the docs layer, not the code: three sites still claimed the runtime supports presence penalty 0.0 only (docs/adding-a-model.md:47-48, dated 2026-09-12, and docs/deepseek-v41-flash-port.md:234 and :892, added 2026-09-25 -- the latter copied the runbook's sentence into its deviations), a limitation the v5.10 release notes of 2026-09-24 had already removed. tools/docs-facts.py checks counts, names and tables, so a prose capability claim that the code no longer backs is exactly what it cannot catch; all three are corrected in d3c3841. DECISION, UNRATIFIED: the cap is gated on `rules == .wire`, matching the stop-string caps and the validator's own doc that the wire's caps exist to protect the engine from a third party's request; holding the facade to it would narrow what an embedder may pass through the public GenerationOptions, which per AGENTS.md needs a recorded decision in docs/plan-embedded-library.md. The operator has been asked whether the -2...2 bound should also apply on the .local path.

tasks.category: interface text: the flag's own help and refusals described a set as a range and named no choices
tasks.file_line: sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/ServerArguments+Usage.swift:38-41
tasks.title: --max-context says "Native: 4096...262144" and refuses 100000; its launcher repeats the promise
tasks.discovered-by: Phase D continuation of the AUD-254 boundary family onto the server's own startup surface: every numeric flag in ServerArguments.swift read for what its guard checks against what its message and its --help line say.
tasks.evidence-before: The gate asks `RuntimeConfiguration.supportedContextTokens.contains(maxContext)` -- seven rungs, 4096 8192 16384 32768 65536 131072 262144 -- and the existing suite pins that 100000 is refused (OpenAIValidationTests.swift:690, `accepts256KContextAndRejectsUnsupportedValues`). Three surfaces described that differently: `--help` printed "Native: 4096...262144", an ellipsis over a set; the refusal at :384 said "--max-context is not supported" and named nothing, while its YaRN sibling two lines above names both of its two choices; and the parse site at :210 shared that same string, so `--max-context abc` (a typo) and `--max-context 2000000` (above the ceiling) both read as a policy refusal. `supportedContextTokens` has exactly one production consumer -- this gate -- so the rungs are a server policy, not an engine constraint, and the refusal text was the only statement of it. Measured by the new test before the repair (/tmp/aud255-red2.log, exit 1, 4 issues at :724 :729 x2 :734): the between-rung refusal contained no list, the two parse-site refusals named no ceiling, and the usage text did not contain the rungs. Blast radius: tools/server_launcher.sh:65 documented `--context <n|native|max>` as a token count and :1086 passed any all-digit value straight through, so `--context 100000` reached the server and died at startup with the message that named no choices.
tasks.evidence-after: The help line and both refusals are spelled from the lists that enforce them and the test asserts against the same source: `swift test --no-parallel --filter ServerArgumentTests` -- 20 tests in 1 suite, exit 0 (/tmp/aud255-green3.log). Full package suite serially: 7 target runs, 1735 tests in 253 suites, exit 0 (/tmp/aud255-full2.log) -- the count is up by the one new test. Gates as `bash tools/lint.sh <mode>`, each exit 0: swift-format, swiftlint, func-length, file-length, test-skip, test-hollow, docs, shell, shellcheck. No test or document elsewhere asserted the old strings (`rg "is not supported"` over tests/ benchmark/ tools/ finds only the new doc comment), and no document copies the old help line. No model run -- the operator's TinyTitanServer holds the only live model process; nothing fetched; nothing pushed.
tasks.fix-evidence: Four mutants, each killed by a different assertion of theContextRefusalNamesTheChoicesTheHelpPromises: (A) usage list hand-written one rung short -> exit 1 at :734, proving the help is derived, not merely formatted to look derived; (B) rung refusal back to "is not supported" -> exit 1 at :724; (C) prefill-chunk help hand-listed without 4096 -> exit 1 at :752; (D) parse-site ceiling message reverted -> exit 1, 2 issues (the "abc" and "2000000" rows). The sibling assertion was written RED first and watched to fail alone (/tmp/aud255-red3.log, exit 1, 1 issue) before --prefill-chunk was changed. Files restored between mutants from copies taken after each edit (/tmp/aud255-*-fixed*.swift), not `git checkout --`; `git diff --stat` before the commit showed only the four intended files.
tasks.sibling-note: Every numeric flag in the same switch read for the same gap. True and fixed beside the named defect: `--prefill-chunk` -- membership test against `allowedPrefillChunkTokens`, refusal said "is not supported" with no list while its `--expert-cache-slots` sibling spells its choices out; both message and help now derive. Measured negatives, not filed: `--mtp-memory-mib`'s "between 256 and 512" is honest because `allowedBudgetMiB` is a ClosedRange, not a set; `--expert-cache-slots` already interpolates its list (brackets and all -- true, cosmetic, untouched); `--kv-bits <4|8|16>` matches `KVCachePrecision`'s three cases; `--max-concurrent-sequences` interpolates `maximumSlots`; `--port`, `--queue-limit`, `--prompt-cache-*` and `--idle-unload-seconds` each name the bound they check. The launcher's `--context` text is corrected but its behaviour is not -- it still passes any token count through, which is right now that the refusal is explicit, and the record notes that the accepted set itself is a policy choice no engine code enforces. `tools/dsh_route.sh`'s `--context <n>` is a different thing: it writes `defaultContextWindow` into the client config (:267, :273) and never reaches the server gate, so a non-rung value there is legal -- checked, not a defect. LEFT OPEN, NOT CHANGED: the CLI accepts any `--max-context` in 1...262144 (Args.swift:262 plus the `else if maxContext > nativeMaximumContextTokens` check at :385) while the server takes the seven rungs, so the scripted verification path can drive a window the server will not start with. Which side moves is a runtime-behaviour decision -- AGENTS.md puts changing accepted configurations to the user -- and is recorded here for the operator rather than guessed at.

tasks.category: observability: a counter was accumulated and never read
tasks.file_line: sources/TinyTitanMemory/MemoryService+Consolidation.swift:172

tasks.evidence-before: `storeConsolidation` declares `var held = 0`, does `held += 1` under `case .held:` (:172) and passes it to `logConsolidationSummary` -- and the parameter was never in the signature. The summary function's own doc comment says "One line per counter that fired", and it covered `unchanged`, `duplicates`, `dropped` (not-durable), `ruleConflicts` and `conflicts`, but had no branch for the guard. The per-key `guardHeld(key:)` line does fire, so the refusal is not silent; what is lost is the aggregate: a consolidation that refused four of five model rewrites logged one disputed line per key and a summary that read like a quiet one, so nothing in the session's log told the operator the guard was carrying the write. No model run -- the operator's TinyTitanServer holds the only live model process; nothing fetched; nothing pushed.
tasks.fix-evidence: Three mutants, each killed with exit 1 (/tmp/aud256-mutant{A,B,C}.log): (A) the `if held > 0` line dropped -> the new test fails, proving the test is attached to the behaviour and not to the log-call refactor; (B) `count: held` replaced with a hardcoded `count: 1` -> fails, proving the number asserted is the number counted; (C) `count: held` replaced with `count: duplicates` -> fails, proving the count is the guard's and not the nearest neighbour's. tasks.category: lifetime: a stop() that does not survive the caller's own background task
tasks.file_line: sources/TinyTitanFleet/Core/FleetScanner.swift:103-127
tasks.title: `FleetScanner.stop()` cleared the in-flight guard, so a scan kicked by the dashboard's action task could dial the LAN after the terminal was restored
tasks.discovered-by: Queue lead carried in from the previous session, where it was filed as a doc-comment defect ("stop()'s doc promises it waits for a scan in flight; the body only cancels"). Reading the caller before writing showed the doc was the smaller half of it.
tasks.evidence-before: `stop()` cancelled `task` and `inFlight` and set both to nil. `requestScan()` guards on `inFlight == nil` only, so after a stop the guard passes again. The reachable path is in the dashboard: `sources/TinyTitanFleet/Command/main.swift:230` runs a mutating action on an untracked `Task { runner.perform(action...); notes.put(...); scanner.requestScan() }` -- nobody holds that task, so teardown does not wait for it -- and `main.swift:236-237` then does `await scanner.stop(); terminal.restore()`. An action that finished after the restore therefore called `requestScan()` on a stopped scanner and started a fresh scan of every peer while the user's shell was back on screen: the process was still alive long enough to open the connections, and the output went to a terminal it no longer owned. Measured before the repair (/tmp/aud257-red.log, exit 1, 1 issue at ScannerTests.swift:294: `await transport.count() == before` -- the count had gone up after the stop).
tasks.evidence-after: `stop()` sets a sticky `private var stopped = false` (:58) that only `requestScan()` honours (`guard !stopped, inFlight == nil else { return }`, :123); `start()` is deliberately not refused, because that is the owner asking to poll again and the flag's doc says so. `stop()` stays synchronous: the header now records that it cancels rather than waits, why a synchronous actor method could not wait (a scan that asked a dead peer sits out the full timeout, so waiting would hold the terminal before `restore()`), and what that costs (an in-flight scan can still publish a snapshot afterwards, which nothing reads at that point) -- the original doc claim of "wait for any scan in flight to finish" is gone rather than left as a promise nothing implements. Verified: `swift test --no-parallel --filter FleetScannerScheduleTests` -- 4 tests in 1 suite, exit 0 (/tmp/aud257-green.log); fleet target 63 tests in 14 suites, exit 0 (/tmp/aud257-fleet.log); full package suite serially: 7 target runs, 1737 tests in 253 suites, exit 0 (/tmp/aud257-full.log). Gates as `bash tools/lint.sh <mode>`, each exit 0: force-cast, unbounded-read, func-length, file-length, sendable, test-skip, test-hollow, stdout-clean, library-facade, arch-path, docs, swift-format, swiftlint. The test drives the in-process `HostTransport` fake -- no socket is opened and no peer is dialled, so the proof does not touch the network.
tasks.fix-evidence: Two mutants, each killed with exit 1 (/tmp/aud257-mutant{A,B}.log): (A) the `stopped` flag set but the `requestScan()` guard left as `inFlight == nil` only -> fails, proving the refusal is the flag and not the nil-clearing; (B) the flag checked on `start()` instead of `requestScan()` -> fails, pinning the asymmetry that the fix chose: the owner's `start()` may resume polling, the stray `requestScan()` may not. tasks.category: decision: a public setter whose documented caller does not exist, and wiring it changes measured performance
tasks.file_line: sources/TinyTitanServer/Core/CPUModelBackend.swift:175
tasks.title: `CPUModelBackend.setContention` promises the caller sets the served CPU model's thread width from GPU activity; no caller does, so in a mixed GPU+CPU catalog the CPU model holds full width while a GPU generation runs
tasks.discovered-by: Section 6 unused-code sweep (`.build/aud258/dead.py`), the second of two survivors; AUD-258 was the other.
tasks.evidence-before: Measured statically, this commit. `rg -n setContention -g '*.swift'` over sources/, tests/, tools/, examples/ and plugins/ returns exactly one line: the definition at CPUModelBackend.swift:175-177. (A plain grep also lit up two Metal `.pcm`/module records under `examples/embedded/.build`; `strings` shows they hold `setContentionRelief`, an unrelated SDK symbol, so those are not callers.) The chain the setter feeds is live and does work elsewhere: `CPUQwen35.applyWidthPolicy()` (:181-184) is called before every token from `step(token:needsLogits:)` (:154), and `guard let contention else { return }` (:182) means a nil signal leaves `threads` at whatever it was. Nothing passes contention to the served backend: `CPUModelBackend.init` builds the engine as `CPUQwen35(snapshot: snapshot)` (:104) with no `threads:` argument, and that constructor's own lines (:101-102) set both `threads` and `idleThreads` to `Int8AffineGEMV.preferredThreads`. The path where the signal *is* installed is the side engine -- `SideEngine.swift:330` does `model.contention = isClientGenerating` on the model it loads in the background -- and main.swift:193 supplies `{ coordinator.generating.isBusy }` for it. The gap is the catalog: `ModelRouter.standardLoader` (:82-102) loads `.gpu` entries as sessions and `.cpu` entries as `CPUModelBackend` in the same server, so a process serving both has a GPU generation and a full-width CPU generation competing for the same performance cores. The cost is this tree's own recorded numbers, quoted in the doc comments at CPUModelBackend.swift:172-174 and CPUQwen35.swift:48-51: one thread costs a 35B generation 3%, two cost 13%, four cost 31%.
tasks.owner: operator -- the choice changes measured runtime performance, which AGENTS.md bars an auditor from making unprompted
tasks.evidence-after: Not changed. Two candidate repairs, and they are not equivalent: (1) wire the served CPU backend to a *GPU-only* busy signal, so it narrows while a GPU generation holds the device and not while it is itself decoding; (2) delete `setContention` and reword the doc to the truth -- the width is caller-set for the side engine, which is the only place it is set, and the served CPU model runs at preferred width. Option (1) is the one the doc asks for and it cannot be written with what exists today: `coordinator.generating` (:27, `enter()`/`leave()` at :65-66) counts every generation without regard to kind, so `backend.setContention { coordinator.generating.isBusy }` would clamp the served CPU model to `busyThreads = 1` during its *own* decode -- a naive wiring that reads as correct and is the wrong semantics. A real fix therefore adds a per-kind busy signal to the coordinator or the router, which is engine-scheduling work with a numerics-adjacent cost, and it needs a model run to measure, which the operator's live server currently bars.
tasks.sibling-note: Checked for the same shape nearby: `CPUQwen35.threads` (:36) is set directly by the benchmark drivers, which is what its doc says, so that one has its caller; `idleThreads`/`busyThreads` (:52+) are read only through `applyWidthPolicy()`, so they stay. `SideEngine.contention`'s getter/setter pair (:401-404) forwards to the engine and is reached through the same :330 install. The setter is `public` on `TinyTitanServerCore`, not inside `TinyTitanLib`, so the `library-facade` gate does not cover it and no gate would have caught an uncalled public method here -- §5's facade allowlist is scoped to the library target by design.
